alan: Heads up — I sketched a short rollout plan for landing paged/Fv2+Fv3 kernel selection and a safe fallback. Opening the thread for feedback.

maya: Nice, can you paste the feature-flag config you had in mind?

alan: Sure. Idea is a single flag + selection table so we can switch kernels per model/seq/KV-enabled. Example:
```
feature_flag: attn.kernel_picker = 'auto'
attn.kernel_picker.table = [
  {model_regex: '.*-redwood-large', kv: true, max_seq: 2048, prefer: 'flashv3'},
  {model_regex: '.*-redwood-small', kv: false, max_seq: 1024, prefer: 'flashv2'},
  {model_regex: '.*', kv: true, max_seq: 4096, prefer: 'paged-fusion'}
]
attn.fallback_policy = ['paged-fusion','flashv2']
rollout.stages = ['staging','canary','ramp']
```

rachel: Two quick asks: 1) how does this interact with the KV cache eviction heuristics? 2) telemetry hooks?

alan: Good ones. For KV we add a small metadata tag on cached entries: `kernel_hint`. When we evict we prefer to evict entries that were created under kernels known to have higher memory churn (currently flashv3 hot spots). Telemetry: we will emit `attn.kernel` + `kv.hit/miss` + `batch_size` + `latency_p50/p95` per request.

tom: We've got a perf regression on long sequences when kv is enabled on fuser branch — saw ~12% p95 increase in staging yesterday. Is that the same area?

alan: Yes, likely related. My profiling shows a hotspot in fused attention's reduction path when KV page stitching happens. Short-term fix is to fall back to flashv2 for sequences > 2048 when kv=true.

infra-bot: deploy check: staging infra has GPUs with cuda 12.2 and sm86; flashv3 kernels require cudnn 9.1. Compatibility flag set to false for nodes without required libs.

maya: Can we make that fallback opt-in per-customer? Some large customers prefer latest kernels despite risks.

alan: We'll add an override map: `rollout.overrides.customer_id = {prefer: 'flashv3', allow_risky: true}` — admin only.

rachel: For metrics, add a diff alert on unit-cost/token and regeneration rate. If error rate or unit-cost jumps >5% during canary, auto-roll back.

deploy-bot: Proposed canary plan: staging smoke -> 3% host-level canary (non-prod) -> 5% production traffic (slices across regions) -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%. Auto-rollback triggers: p95 latency +5%, error-rate +0.5pp, unit-cost +7%.

sre-kate: Add a runbook step: if p95 regressions persist after rollback, force kernel-picker to `flashv2` globally and open P1. Also add continuous profiler on the canary hosts for 48h.

tom: I can instrument a small microbenchmark that simulates KV paging + variable batch sizes. Will post results by EOD.

alan: Thanks. Action items:
- tom: microbench + upload flamegraphs -> due today 18:00
- maya: write feature flag schema -> due tomorrow AM
- rachel: alert thresholds + dashboards -> due tomorrow lunchtime
- infra: ensure compat tags on nodes -> asap
- alan: implement picker + fallback + telemetry -> PR by Monday

maya: pinging @alan on the picker interface — will need a simple API to override per-customer in console.

alan: yup, will add a minimal admin endpoint: `POST /admin/attn/overrides` with `customer_id` and `policy`.

rachel: One more thing — include a perf budget in the PR description (target p95 delta < 2% vs baseline for 95% of models).

alan: noted. I'll link the benchmark harness and include the budget.

tom: quick profiling note: with batch_size=8 and seq=3072 + kv page stitching, hotspot shows 30% more DRAM traffic and 10% CPU spin on memcpy. Might be a kernel memory layout issue.

alan: OK, that explains the p95 regression. If microbench confirms, plan B is to add a small memcpy coalescing path in the paged-fusion kernel. If that's risky, fallback policy remains.

rachel: LGTM. If no objections I'll merge the canary gating playbook into ops-docs after we get the microbench results.

alan: Thanks all. Will keep updates in this thread.

[thread closed for now — will reopen when tom posts flamegraphs]
